questions.q: Which safety procedures must I follow before maintenance on this machine?
questions.answer:
Before any maintenance on MCH-0001, the manual (page 33) requires:

- **Isolate all energy sources** and dissipate residual energies — this must be done by qualified technicians.
- **Pneumatic energy:** put the slider valve in the discharge position and lock it there.
- **Tools:** wrenches and tools used for maintenance or access to hazardous sections must not be left available to untrained operators.

After the work, before restarting (page 33):

- Check that replaced parts and tools have been removed from the machine.
- Check that all guards, protections and safety devices removed during the intervention are correctly re-installed and operating.
- Electrical safety components must be replaced within their life cycle (approx. 20 years).

Also note (page 24): any intervention on electric and/or pneumatic equipment is forbidden for personnel without the specific technical knowledge and training required.

questions.q: Why is machine 15610 generating repeated alarms?
questions.answer:
Here's what the last 30 days show for MCH-0001 (serial 15610, twin-chute capper, 20 heads / 40,000 bph):

**The repeated alarms cluster around the caps feeding system:**
- **AL082_MINIMUM_CAPS_LEVEL** (Low) – 5×, last 2026-07-30
- **AL016_CAPS_CHUTE_FULL** (Low) – 4×, last 2026-08-03
- **AL023_CAPS_CHECK_INTERVENTION** (Medium) – 4×, last 2026-08-03
- **AL074_OVERTURNED_CAPS_CHECK** (Medium) – 4×, 1 still open, last 2026-08-03
- **AL017_LOW_AIR_PRESSURE** (High) – 4×, 1 still open, last 2026-07-29

**Plus repeated emergency stops:** AL086_LINE_EMERGENCY_PRESSED (Critical) 4× (2 still open) and AL024_FRONT_PANEL_EMERGENCY_PRESSED (Critical) 3× (1 still open), all around 2026-07-22 to 2026-07-29.

**What this means:** the chute is starving and clogging alternately (minimum level + chute full), and the air that drives the caps is weak — the manual's fault table (p. 152) points to a clogged sorter exit mouth and incorrect air-jet pressure as the first things to check, and p. 46 (twin-hopper feeding) explains the machine switches to the second chute when the first runs dry or the transfer-disc photocell misfires. The low-air-pressure alarms fit: p. 97 requires checking supply pressure, pressure reducers, condensate and filter clogging every 40 working hours. The emergency presses look like operators stopping the line to clear the jams.

Suggested first checks: clean the sorter exit mouth and chute, verify air pressure at the gauges and drain/replace the filter, then inspect the caps presence photocells and transfer-disc timing (p. 146).

questions.q: What does AL017_LOW_AIR_PRESSURE mean and what does the manual recommend?
questions.answer:
I searched the manual for AL017 but found no dedicated entry for that alarm code, so I can only tell you what the name indicates plus the manual's air-pressure guidance:

- **Meaning:** the pneumatic system's air pressure has dropped below the working pressure set on the machine.
- **Manual recommendations (pneumatic system checks, p. 97 and p. 98):**
  - Check the air supply pressure at the utilization points and verify the pressure reducers are set to the work pressure (value shown on the gauges).
  - Drain condensate from under the discharge filter and check the filter for clogging; replace if needed.
  - Check for leaks at fittings and lines, and verify the air pressure at the machine entry matches the data plate.
- **Related note (p. 88):** if caps are not correctly shifted by the nozzles, adjust the air pressure with the fitting pressure reducers.

If you want, I can pull the recent AL017 occurrences on MCH-0001 to see when and how often it has fired.
